name: NY-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+22 partisan lean in deep-blue Brooklyn
Incumbent Yvette Clarke running with roughly $1 million raised versus an unreported-finance challenger
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No polls or expert ratings, leaving fundamentals as the main evidence
model.rationale: Clarke's incumbency in a D+22 Brooklyn district, a large fundraising edge, and markets pricing her near 96 percent all point to an overwhelming Democratic margin, so the forecast stays at roughly D+26. The uncertainty band is somewhat wide only because no public polls cover the race.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal involving Clarke or a surge of outside spending for Azumah could narrow the expected margin, though nothing of the kind has surfaced.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Yvette Clarke, the Democratic incumbent in this Brooklyn-based House district, enters the general election as a heavy favorite. The district's D+22 partisan lean, her status as a long-serving incumbent, and a substantial fundraising advantage over Republican Joel Azumah, who shows no reported campaign finance activity, leave little structural opening for an upset. Clarke has also drawn outside support on her behalf.

No public polling or expert ratings cover the race, so the assessment rests on fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets, which put the Democratic win probability near 96 percent. The expected margin is roughly 26 points, with modest uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, consistent with its consistently strong Democratic performance in recent cycles.
